issue.title: Nested preservation leaks PermissionError instead of its typed refusal on Python 3.12/3.13
issue.description: Found by sase-1ou.6.land--3 while auditing the post-repair scheduled Full CI runs 40976564464 (f94ad24a4a) and 41011050293 (20dc76bd09). Both contain the Files repair but this failure is independent. Exact excerpts: file:explicit:26a0e166c4b017177f87eabb. All-status exact/semantic searches and past-week task sweep found no duplicate; reviewed active epics and found no demonstrated causal owner. Normalize filesystem permission failures around the Git-marker probe into the documented PreservationError, preserving refusal and nested-work safety. Add cross-version regression coverage without relaxing the exception assertion. Source predates this Files epic; this is distinct from slot quarantine policy (sase-1p9).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Repeated on both scheduled runs on Python 3.12 and 3.13. In _snapshot_nested.py::_collect_git_roots, git_marker.exists() raises PermissionError for the mode-0 sase/repos directory before the guarded iterdir block can convert it to PreservationError. Python 3.14 differs in pathlib error handling.

issue.creation_reason: Two scheduled CI audits independently expose this failure outside the Files navigation epic; record it for repair without blocking that epic.
